text:
maya: Pager alert — NAT ephemeral port exhaustion in us-west-2 at 18:12 UTC. spikes of connection resets and model-pull failures seen. errors: curl: (56) recv failure: Connection reset by peer

liam: looking at cloudwatch now. outbound tcp TIME_WAIT counts on the NAT ENIs are huge.

sara: Is this tied to the nightly model rollout that started ~18:00?

jordan: yes — rollout kicked off a simultaneous pull job on every pod. each pull opens lots of short-lived connections to model-registry.s3. we hit ~40-60k TIME_WAIT per AZ.

devex: temporary mitigation: can we route model pulls through the internal cache (model-cache.redwood.internal)? we already have cached artifacts there but rollout uses direct S3 URL.

liam: confirmed: `netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` returned 53240 on one of the nat instances. also seeing a flurry of `ECONNRESET` in agent logs and envoy upstream connection failures.

maya: quick ops plan: 1) pause rollout 2) throttle pull concurrency 3) switch pulls to cache proxy 4) create one extra NAT gateway per AZ as short-term capacity increase.

jordan: pausing rollout now (controller -> set maxUnavailable=95%). pushing a stop to the job.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created and assigned to eng-infra. Priority: P2.

sara: for a longer-term fix we should: - enable VPC S3 endpoint for registry traffic - bake model tarballs into AMIs or node-local cache - move heavy fanout pulls to a single inbound proxy with connection pooling (envoy/http keepalive)

devex: +1 on connection pooling. most SDKs do new TCP per download by default. switching to persistent connection pools or using `requests.Session()` (python) and `maxIdleConns` (go) will drastically cut ephemeral usage.

liam: I can spin up a small envoy proxy on a few nodes to KISS-swap pulls to a pooled connection out via NAT; will try that as an immediate relief while infra adds NATGW.

maya: liam please also add a quick metric on ephemeral ports per nat-gw and an alert at >45k. we had none configured.

jordan: creating infra change: request to add 3rd NAT gateway in each AZ and increase route table association to new TGWs. putting change in the maintenance window in 30m.

infra-bot: Change request CR-9876 submitted for NAT Gateway add; will execute 00:55 UTC.

sara: also open a ticket for model-registry to serve via internal endpoint (avoid public S3 egress). it's a low-friction win.

devex: small code snippet to reduce ports in python clients: ```python
s = requests.Session()
with s.get(url, stream=True) as r:
    r.raw.read()
```

liam: after pausing and routing some pulls through cache proxy, connection resets dropped by ~70% in the last 10m. CW graphs show TIME_WAIT trending down from 58k to ~18k on that nat.

maya: good. keep throttle on rollout and proceed with the multi-pronged plan. action owners: jordan (NATGW add), liam (proxy quick deploy + metrics), sara (S3 endpoint + registry ticket), devex (client lib guidance + PR).

jordan: added action items to INC-2026-045 and linked to CR-9876.

maya: thanks. we'll reconvene in 30m for status. :thumbsup:

liam: will post logs and netstat snapshots in the incident thread once proxy is up.

infra-bot: Monitoring alert resolved (partial) — downstream 502s reduced after throttle. Keep watch for next hour.

sara: noting cost implication: extra NAT gateways will add some monthly fixed cost, but reducing failed retries will likely save egress and compute. I'll put a rough cost note in the ticket.

maya: final: be careful with rollouts that fan out to public endpoints. default concurrency patterns need to be workload-aware. documenting as postmortem checklist.

devex: adding a short-run doc with best-practices for model pull patterns and client pools. linking here when ready.

maya: closing for now — status OK for next check.
